title: Let's Carry the Big Box Together
theme: Asking for help and working together (cooperation)
blurb: Ali wants to make a playhouse out of a great big box, but the box won't even budge. He takes a deep breath and asks his friends for help; with Elif's idea, “One, two, three, all together!”, the box lifts into the air.

pages.text: Ali's dad brought a great big box to the park. Thump! The box landed on the grass. The box was even bigger than Ali! Ali went hop, hop, hop: “I'm going to make a playhouse!”

ali.say: I'm going to make a playhouse!

baba.say: The big box is yours, Ali!

pages.ask: What would you do with a great big box?

pages.text: Ali pushed the box. Hnnngh! It didn't move. He pulled. Hnnngh! Still nothing. Ali felt fed up. His cheeks grew hot. “Too heavy! I can't do it!”

ali.say: Hnnngh! It's too heavy! I can't do it!

pages.ask: How is Ali feeling now? What do you do when you can't do something?

pages.text: Zeynep came running. Elif's wheels went whirr, whirr. Ali took a deep breath. “Can you help me?” “Of course!” said Zeynep. “I have an idea!” said Elif.

predict.q: What do you think Elif's idea is?
predict.res: Good idea! Let's see what Elif has in mind.

pages.ask: What did Ali say to ask for help? Who do you ask for help?

pages.text: Ali held one end. Zeynep held the other end. Elif counted: “One, two, three, all together!” Upsy-daisy! The box lifted into the air!

mech.done: All together! The box lifted into the air!

pages.hint: Count with Elif: one, two, three!
pages.ask: Why did they count all together before lifting the box?

pages.text: “This way!” said Elif. Ali and Zeynep carried the box. Pitter patter. Step, step, all together!
pages.hint: Touch Elif so she shows the way!
pages.ask: How do we walk when we carry something heavy together? Let's try it: step, step!

pages.text: The box landed under the tree. Everyone brought something: a cushion, a teddy, a book. All into the playhouse!

mech.done: The playhouse is ready! How lovely it looks!

pages.hint: Carry the things into the box!
pages.ask: What would you put in the playhouse? Why?

pages.text: Ali hid behind the box. Peekaboo! The three friends giggled: tee-hee-hee! Ali said, “Thank you!” Elif smiled: “When we're together, even a box feels light!”

ali.say: Peekaboo! Here I am! Thank you!

elif.say: When we're together, even a box feels light!

pages.ask: Who did you last do a job with? How did you feel?

kazanim: HSAB.6 Showing movement patterns in harmony with a partner/group (learning outcome): lifts at the same time as friends to the count “One, two, three, all together!” and walks “step, step” in the same rhythm.
HSAB.1.c Performs movements that require object control (learning outcome): carries a large object with a friend, each holding one end (in class, with light, empty boxes).

SBAB5 Social Participation (domain skill) and SDB2.2 Cooperation: joins in the shared job of building a playhouse; asks friends for help with a job they cannot do alone, and notices that each friend takes on a task (holding, counting, showing the way, bringing things).
E2.5 Playfulness: makes up a game with friends from a simple object like a cardboard box, and enriches the game by adding things to it.
D20 Helpfulness and D4 Friendship: answers a friend who asks for help with “Of course!”; says thank you after being helped.
once: Show an empty, large cardboard box: “What could this box be? Can you carry it by yourself?”
Introduce the children on the cover: “These are Ali, Zeynep and Elif. What do you think they'll do with the great big box?”
Ask: “Has there been a job you couldn't do by yourself? What did you do then?”
sirasi: On page 2, point to Ali's face: “Ali felt fed up, his cheeks grew hot. What happens in your body when you feel fed up?” Take a deep breath together.
On page 3, repeat Ali's sentence with the children: “Can you help me?” For the prediction question, point out that both choices are ways of asking for help: you can ask a friend or a grown-up.

On page 4, count out loud all together with the children: “One, two, three, all together!” and raise your hands into the air together. On page 5, say “Step, step, all together!” and march on the spot hand in hand, in the same rhythm.
sonra: Have the child tell the events in order: Ali couldn't lift the box alone → he asked for help → they counted and lifted it all together → they built the playhouse.
Ask “Who did what?”: Ali held one end, Zeynep held the other end, Elif counted and showed the way. Talk about how every job mattered.
Find sentences together for asking for and accepting help: “Can you help me?”, “Of course!”, “Thank you!”

sinif.materyal: Empty, light, large cardboard boxes (empty inside, corners taped), cushions, small toys
adim: The children split into groups of two or three. Each group holds a box by its two ends.
The teacher or a child from the group counts: “One, two, three, all together!” The group lifts the box at the same time and carries it to the other corner of the room, saying “step, step”.
The groups build their own playhouses by putting cushions and toys in the boxes; each child brings one thing.
To finish, ask each group: “Who did what? How did you feel doing it together?”

evSoru: How did Ali feel when he couldn't lift the box by himself? What did he do next?
What was Elif's idea? How did the box lift into the air?
Who do you do jobs together with at home?

evEtk.ad: Let's Carry It Together at Home
evEtk.d: At home, hold something light but big (a folded blanket, an empty box, the laundry basket) by its two ends with your child. Say “One, two, three, all together!”, lift at the same time and carry it together saying “step, step”. Then build a little playhouse together out of a box or a blanket.

guide.aileNotu: Today we read “Let's Carry the Big Box Together.” Ali wants to make a playhouse out of a great big box, but he can't lift it by himself. He takes a deep breath and asks his friends for help; with Elif's idea, “One, two, three, all together!”, they carry the box together and build the playhouse. At home, you can use sentences for asking for help and saying thank you while doing small jobs together with your child.
